content.text: Occurs when the cord extends past the presenting part of the fetus & protrudes into the vagina
A prolapsed cord can lead to reduced fetal oxygenation as a result of umbilical artery vasospasm &/or umbilical vein occlusion
Risk Factors: low birth weight, malpresentation, long umbilical cord, pelvic deformities, low-lying placentation, polyhydramnios, prematurity
Sudden onset of severe, prolonged fetal bradycardia or variable decelerations after a previously normal tracing
The cord may be palpable on vaginal examination
Visualization or palpation of the cord
U/S may show cord interposed between presenting part of fetus and maternal internal os
Color flow doppler can clarify cord position
Emergent c-section to avoid fetal compromise or death
Preoperative intrauterine resuscitation: manual elevation of the fetal presenting part to prevent compression, placing the pt in the Trendelenburg or knee-chest position
Tocolytics – reduce pressure on cord from uterine contractions
